title: Evaluation and validation of a precision medicine platform in neurodegenerative disease
summary: Clinical decision support systems (CDSS) using artificial intelligence (AI) can help clinicians understand complex diagnostic data and manage patients' disease progression. CDSSs could improve diagnostic pathways of patients and address the shortage of specialists in Europe. As new Alzheimer's treatments emerge, there will be a greater need for efficient diagnostic pathways. This study consists of two sub-projects, an Evaluation study (Part A) and a Validation study (Part B). In Part A, we will look at what individuals think about the use of a CDSS in the memory clinic, how easy it is to use, what benefits it offers and what challenges it presents. We will do this with clinicians, patients and caregivers in seven memory clinics across Europe. PROMINENT will also create a training programme for the CDSS. To test the CDSS in Part B, PROMINENT will analyse if its use can improve the diagnostic process and use fewer resources without affecting how confident clinicians are in their diagnoses. The study will also analyse the performance of the CDSS (validation study).
conditions: Dementia in other diseases classified elsewhere
Other specified degenerative diseases of nervous system

interventions.name: The objective of Part A (Evaluation study) is to assess attitudes towards the utilisation of a clinical decision support software (CDSS), encompassing aspects such as user-friendliness, design, content and satisfaction with the tool and the reports generated. This will be assessed via questionnaires

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Part A (Evaluation study)

Clinicians
- 18 years or older
- Ability to provide written informed consent
- Actively involved in the diagnostic process for neurodegenerative diseases
- Ability to speak and read English fluently

Patients
- 45 years or older
- Underwent diagnostics at the memory clinic
- Ability to provide written informed consent
- Ability to read and fluently speak the local language or English for study
assessments

Care partners
- 18 years or older
- Ability to provide written informed consent
- Ability to read and fluently speak the local language or English for study
assessments

Part B (Validation study)

Clinicians
- 18 years or older
- Ability to provide written informed consent
- Actively involved in the diagnostic process for neurodegenerative diseases
- Ability to speak and read English fluently

Patients
- 45 years or older
- Underwent diagnostics at the memory clinic
- Ability to provide written informed consent
- Underwent neuropsychological testing including CERAD/RAVLT word list, TMT
A+B, animal fluency within the last six months
- Brain MRI available (T1 MPRAGE with slice thickness <1.5mm, T2 FLAIR, T2* or
SWI; 1.5 or 3 Tesla), not older than 12 months
Exclusion criteria:
Part A and B (Evaluation study and validation study)
Patients:
- Any major medical condition that according to clinical judgement hinders
communication and participation in the study activities, e.g. major psychiatric
conditions, alcohol or substance abuse, brain tumors
- Impaired ability to provide written informed consent as per clinical judgement
according to local standard procedures
